findings.evidence: Mathlib's canonical API exposes all three parallel forms at `EulerProduct.eulerProduct_hasProd` (Basic.lean:175), `EulerProduct.eulerProduct` (Basic.lean:210), and `EulerProduct.eulerProduct_tprod` (Basic.lean:225); this PR exposes only the first and third at lines 100/127 and 105/125.
findings.fix: Add the generic `Tendsto (fun n ↦ ∏ p ∈ Nat.primesBelow n, …) Filter.atTop (𝓝 (LSeries a s))` theorem and its `Eigenform.LSeries_eulerProduct` specialization.
findings.issue: Only `HasProd` and `tprod` forms are exposed; there is no `LSeries_eulerProduct_of_recurrence` theorem expressing convergence of products over `Nat.primesBelow`, and the eigenform specialization has the same gap at `LFunction/EulerProduct.lean:105`.

summary: The Euler-product API omits the canonical finite-partial-product convergence form provided by the underlying Mathlib API.
